transcript:
Meeting Header
Date: 2025-04-16
Time: 3:00 PM PT
Duration: 45 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Samir Patel (Redwood SE), Jordan Lee (Acme ML - ML Eng), Priya Narang (Acme ML - Head of ML), Carlos Mendez (Acme ML - CTO)

Auto-summary: quick review of the last week's bench marks, focus on cost per token economics and what to tune for next week.

[00:00] Maya (Redwood AE): okay good afternoon everyone, thanks for joining, let's jump in, we have about 45 minutes, main goal is a quick review of the cost per token economics and the caching + batching experiments.
[00:15] Jordan (Customer): yeah thanks, we want to validate the numbers we saw last week and figure out if dedicated capacity makes sense long term or whether host it is fine.
[00:30] Samir (Redwood SE): right, and we brought the updated benchmark spreadsheet, I put together tokens per second per dollar metrics across the model variants and quantization profiles. I'll share screen after the recap, but high level \u2014 dedicated gives you ~3x tokens/sec per dollar compared to hosted at current configs, largely due to reserved GPU utilization and bulk kernel selection.
[00:50] Priya (Customer): when you say 3x, is that with batching on? we care about p95/p99 for user-facing flows so can't just blast big batches.
[01:05] Samir: good call, these numbers are with a conservative batching policy that caps latency at ~200ms p95. If you relaxed it to 500ms you see higher tokens/sec per dollar, but p99 climbs. We tried two configs: batch size of 8 (low latency) and batch size of 64 (high throughput).
[01:25] Carlos (Customer): curious about caching, your last note said we could save 30-50% token cost with prefix caching. That seems high, how realistic is that for our traffic?
[01:40] Samir: yeah that depends on prefix reuse. With your conversational templates where users often start with the same system prompt and a handful of repeated phrases, our K-V cache captured about 35% of token generation on the sample workload. On the replay we did, peak savings hit ~48% during repeating flows but sustained average was ~33-36%. Note: sometimes the transcripting here says K-V cash, I mean K-V cache, sorry.
[02:05] Jordan: the replay we ran last Wednesday had higher repetition, maybe that's inflating savings, we'll run a longer 24h replay on staging.
[02:20] Maya: perfect. On tokens/sec per dollar, to put numbers on the table \u2014 in our bench you're looking at roughly 1.1k tokens/sec per $ for hosted with the curated open model quantized to int8 and conservative batching; dedicated goes to ~3.4k tokens/sec per $ for the same model family when pinned to a reserved GPU pool. These are ballpark and will change with sequence length and prompt mix.
[02:45] Priya: can you show how sequence length affects that? our median is 120 tokens but tail goes to 800 when we do long summaries.
[03:00] Samir: absolutely, we plotted cost vs avg sequence length. Shorter sequences get more efficiency from batching because you can fill more slots per batch. For long sequences the KV cache helps more because you avoid redoing the prompt prefix, but per-token kernel efficiency drops a bit.
[03:20] Jordan: any weird stuff about model variants \u2014 like if we switch to a smaller Llama derivative we lose quality, does that tradeoff look better cost wise?
[03:35] Samir: smaller models are cheaper per token but quality regression varies by task. We recommended trying the 13B variant with 4-bit quant as a middle ground in the spreadsheet \u2014 it improved tokens/sec per $ by ~60% over the 70B at a measurable but acceptable quality drop on your eval prompts. We'll put the eval curves in the shared sheet.
[03:55] Carlos: we need to keep SLOs, so how does batching impact p99?
[04:10] Samir: batching increases throughput but it adds queuing latency. For example, going from batch=8 to batch=32 increased throughput 2.5x but p99 latency went from ~320ms to ~820ms in our lab under bursty load. Using adaptive batching with latency caps helps \u2014 Redwood can enforce a per-route latency cap which will flush batches early.
[04:35] Priya: is that a runtime thing or do we need to tune Kube-ernetes?
[04:45] Samir: runtime-level, it's handled by the serving runtime \u2014 you can configure target latency and it will adjust batch flush thresholds. Airing note: sometimes the auto transcript writes cube- erneteres, weird.
[04:58] Jordan: on caching \u2014 what's needed on our side to enable prefix caching? Is it just sending the same prompt IDs or do we need to change client code?
[05:10] Maya: two options: 1) identical prompt strings will be cached automatically by prefix matching, no code change; 2) for more control, you can send a cache-key header (we support a client-side cache key) so you can normalize prompts and increase hit rate. We'll document both.
[05:30] Jordan: good. Also curious about batch vs cache interplay \u2014 if you have strong caching will batching still help as much?
[05:40] Samir: caching reduces generated tokens, which reduces opportunities for batching on generation tokens but still helps because you shorten the compute path \u2014 net effect is you get multiplicative savings: saved tokens reduce per-request compute and batching improves throughput on the remaining tokens. In some configs heavy caching reduced required batch sizes for cost parity.
[06:05] Priya: we ran a quick cost projection and wanted to compare hosted vs dedicated with our projected Q3 traffic \u2014 can you comment on break-even points?
[06:18] Maya: yes break-even depends on committed utilization. In our model sheet we assume your Q3 baseline of 100M tokens/day. With that, dedicated becomes cost-effective if you average >55% GPU utilization on the reserved pool. We'll share the exact threshold numbers in the spreadsheet.
[06:40] Carlos: what's the operational overhead for dedicated \u2014 like autoscaling, burst capacity, SLAs?
[06:50] Maya: Dedicated has autoscale policies, bursts into a shared pool for short windows, and SLA-backed uptime. For initial POC you can start hosted and then switch to dedicated when you lock traffic patterns. We can also set up a hybrid routing \u2014 hot traffic to dedicated and overflow to hosted.
[07:10] Jordan: one more on security \u2014 we need SOC2 and KMS for keys, how does private deployment factor?
[07:20] Samir: Private gives you VPC connectivity and KMS integration; audit logs are available. For the POC we used hosted with encrypted-at-rest and opt-in audit trails; if you need on-prem we can move to Private but that adds setup time. We'll share security addendum docs.
[07:40] Priya: please send the security pack and the SOC2 cert.
[07:45] Maya: will do.
[07:48] Jordan: any surprises in the recent benchmark we should call out?
[07:54] Samir: small one \u2014 there was a noisy neighbor effect in one run where a background CUDA context leaked cycles; we re-ran and smoothed the numbers. Also the replay had higher repetition than prod so caching savings are slightly optimistic.
[08:12] Carlos: okay cool. For the experiments next week can we list concrete configs to try?
[08:20] Samir: yes: 1) staging 24h traffic replay with prefix normalization and caching enabled; 2) two batch configs (latency-focused batch size 8 w/ adaptive flush) and throughput-focused batch size 32 with 500ms cap; 3) try 13B int4 quant variant vs current 70B int8 to compare quality/cost. We'll log p50/p95/p99 and tokens/sec/$ for each.
[08:50] Jordan: I can run the replay, Samir please provide the exact replay tool command and any env flags.
[08:58] Samir: will put that in the sheet.
[09:02] Priya: timeline \u2014 when can we expect the updated spreadsheet?
[09:05] Maya: I'll send by Friday 2025-04-18 with the detailed benchmark and pricing.
[09:10] Jordan: and we'll return logs by 2025-04-22.

Recap / Next Steps
[09:25] Maya: recap: Maya sends updated benchmark/pricing sheet by 4/18; Samir prepares p99 latency tuning notes and replay command; Jordan runs 24h staging replay with prefix caching by 4/22 and shares logs; we reconvene next weekly sync same time unless we need an interim p99 dive.
[09:45] Carlos: sounds good, thanks everyone.

Notes: occasional transcription errors present (K-V cash/KV cache, cube-erneteres/Kubernetes). Attachments referenced: "benchmark_spreadsheet_v2.xlsx" (will be shared), "security_addendum.pdf" (to be shared).
